title: Micro-interactions that make React apps feel faster
description: Loading states, hover intent, focus treatment, and transition timing that improve perceived quality.
hero: Speed is not only a network metric. Interfaces feel faster when they acknowledge user intent, reveal hierarchy clearly, and avoid jarring layout shifts.

sections.heading: Motion should explain state
body: The best micro-interactions are functional. They confirm that a control is interactive, show that content has changed, or guide attention to the next useful area.
Hover lift, focus rings, skeleton states, and subtle transitions can make a product feel more responsive without adding visual noise.

sections.heading: Protect layout stability
body: A fast animation cannot save a layout that jumps. I prefer fixed media ratios, predictable control sizes, and reserved space for loading or empty states.
This is especially important in dashboards, cards, and grids where users scan repeatedly.

sections.heading: Respect reduced motion
body: Motion preferences are part of accessibility. If a user asks for reduced motion, the interface should reduce or remove non-essential transitions.
This portfolio uses a reduced-motion media query so the experience stays usable for more people.

takeaways: Reserve space to prevent layout jumps.
